# Three consumers hand-roll a native route check weaker than Main's

## Context

ADR 0029 §2.8.5 already specifies this authority chain. Focus, position, resize and close

> *"resolve the topology entry inside the App Worker, route the opaque key to the exact owning main thread, and revalidate the live generation before touching the native handle."*

The **main-thread half** is implemented and correct: `src/Main.mjs:783` `#getNativeWindowRoute(data, capability)`, called at eight sites across all four capabilities. The **App-Worker half** — resolving the topology entry and deciding whether this caller may ask at all — has no public owner. So every caller that needs it wrote its own, and each one is weaker than `Main`'s.

Surfaced while mapping #18460's vessel surface ([AC-1 map part 2](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18460#issuecomment-5590783451), [effects layer](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18460#issuecomment-5591493463)). It is the named engine prerequisite blocking that leaf's native bucket; @neo-gpt-emmy, who stewards the consumer epic #18456, declined to fold it there and asked for its own engine authority after a duplicate sweep (that sweep is attested at the foot of this body).

## The Problem

`capabilities?.<capability> === true` guards, enumerated across `src` (492 files), `apps` (317), `examples` (418), `test` (570), `buildScripts` (88):

| file | capability-guard sites | realm |
|---|---:|---|
| `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` | 10 | App Worker |
| `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.mjs` | 6 | App Worker |
| `src/ai/client/RuntimeService.mjs` | 3 | App Worker |
| **total** | **19 across 3 files** | |

`src/dashboard/dock/window/Placement.mjs:306-311` also reads `nativeRoute`, but compares route *identity* (`WindowManager.get(windowId)?.nativeRoute === route`) rather than guarding a capability. Different kind; counted separately and deliberately not swept into this ticket.

**Two of the three are dock consumers. The third is not.** `src/ai/client/RuntimeService.mjs` is engine-side Brain client code, three realms away from docking, and it hand-rolls the same shape at `:316-329` (close), `:370-383` (position), `:412-424` (focus) — destructure `nativeRoute`, test `capabilities?.<cap>`, rebuild `{nativeHandleKey, targetWindowId, windowId: ownerWindowId}`. **A predicate re-derived independently inside `src/` by a subsystem with no relationship to the dock is the evidence that this is engine mechanism, not consumer style.**

### Why the duplication is not merely redundant — it is asymmetrically weaker

`Main.mjs:783` refuses on **six** conditions and repairs state as a side effect:

```js
if (
    !route || route.targetWindowId !== targetWindowId ||
    this.openWindows[entry.windowName] !== entry ||
    entry.win.closed || entry.nativeCapabilities[capability] !== true ||
    typeof entry.win[methods[capability]] !== 'function'
) {
    entry?.win?.closed && this.#invalidateNativeWindowEntry(entry);
    return null
}
```

A consumer's version tests two (`apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:2414`):

```js
route.targetWindowId !== entry.windowId || route.capabilities?.position !== true || …
```

So a consumer can pass its own guard, dispatch, and be refused downstream by a condition it never checked — same-name reuse having replaced the entry, the window being closed, or the native method being absent. **The refusal is real, arrives after dispatch, and looks like nothing.** That is the same silent-refusal class this subsystem keeps producing (`#18455`, `#18448`).

⚠️ **The fix is NOT to give consumers `Main`'s function.** Three of `Main`'s six conditions read main-thread state (`entry.win.closed`, the live `WindowProxy`, method existence) that the App Worker cannot see and must not pretend to. The gap is that nothing owns the checks the App Worker *can* make authoritatively, so each caller invented a subset.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/manager/Window.mjs` is already the App-Worker-side entry owner ADR 0029 §2.8.5 names — *"`manager.Window` remains the runtime topology and geometry observer. Its private entry may carry the reconnect-bounded `{targetWindowId, ownerWindowId, opaqueHandleKey}` route plus generic capability facts."*
- It already holds the data and already **fails closed**: `:151` stores `capabilities: nativeRoute?.capabilities || {close: false, focus: false, position: false, resize: false}`, `:155` stores the `nativeRoute` itself, `:207` nulls the route on disconnect.
- Its public surface is `getWindowAt`, `calculateGeometry`, the three lifecycle handlers and `toJSON` — **no route-authority accessor**. The data is present; the question has no method.
- ADR 0029 §2.8.5 also binds the failure mode: *"Independently opened, cross-origin, stale, or uncorrelated windows remain inspectable where possible but fail closed for physical control."*

## The Fix

Give the App-Worker-side route-authority question one public owner, and route all three callers through it.

**Evidenced candidate: `Neo.manager.Window`.** It is the entry owner in the ADR, it already normalizes the capability facts fail-closed, and the predicate needs nothing it does not already hold. *Falsifier that would move it:* if the predicate turns out to need dock- or vessel-specific state to answer, `manager.Window` is the wrong home — §2.8.5 forbids dock semantics entering the manager — and it belongs in a `src/dashboard/dock/window/` module instead, with `RuntimeService` then needing a separate answer.

**Alternative considered — publish `Main`'s predicate.** Rejected: it answers a main-thread question. Exposing it would either force a round trip per pre-check or invite consumers to cache main-thread truth in the App Worker, which is the staleness ADR 0029 §2.8.5 exists to prevent.

Deliberately **not** prescribing a file, class name or superclass here. #18460's own history is the reason: its earlier prescription named a class and a file before establishing the responsibility's semantic owner and was withdrawn as `ticket-prescription-off`. The responsibility is named above; the implementer establishes the owner against it.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029` (§2.8.5). This implements a step the accepted record already specifies and does not amend it: `Main` remains the physical-handle owner, close remains a separately owner-granted post-commit effect, and the fail-closed rule for stale or uncorrelated windows is what the predicate enforces rather than relaxes. No ADR change is sought; if the implementation finds it must relax any §2.8.5 clause, that is a stop-and-amend, not a judgement call at implementation time.

## Acceptance Criteria

Each criterion names the world in which it goes red, because an AC that cannot fail is not a criterion.

- [ ] A single public App-Worker predicate answers the route-authority question for all four capabilities. *Red today:* no such method exists — `manager.Window`'s public surface is `getWindowAt`, `calculateGeometry`, three lifecycle handlers and `toJSON`.
- [ ] It refuses on each axis independently, one spec per axis: no entry, entry without `nativeRoute`, `ownerWindowId` mismatch, `targetWindowId` mismatch, capability not granted. *Red:* an implementation that returns a route when the caller does not own the window — a single combined assertion would pass while four axes go unchecked, so the ACs are per-axis by construction.
- [ ] All 19 guard sites across the three files route through it; the count of `capabilities?.<cap>` literals in those files reaches zero. *Red today:* 19. `Placement.mjs:306-311` is out of scope and its identity compare must survive untouched.
- [ ] A caller can distinguish "refused before dispatch" from "dispatched and refused by `Main`". *Red:* a bare boolean return, which reproduces the current silent-refusal class in one place instead of three.
- [ ] No spec weakened, and **no tier moved from green to red by this change** — Workstation unit + NL, DemoB unit, `RuntimeService`. Arms already failing on the merge base are excepted **only** where the PR names them and a control run at that base reproduces them, and the PR must not claim they are green. Every behavioural delta is named in the PR body. Refusals may only get **stricter**: a well-formed route behaves identically, and a route missing a required identity refuses earlier — never the reverse. *Red:* a spec edited to accommodate the predicate; a delta the PR body did not name; **any input the old guard refused and the new one admits**; or a baseline failure asserted as green.

  > **Author correction, 2026-09-09.** This criterion originally read *"Zero behavioural change in all three consumers"*. That was imprecise at filing and fought AC-1: routing three consumers through one predicate necessarily makes the two that checked fewer axes refuse cases they previously passed to `Main`, so a literal zero-delta bar could only be met by not delivering the ticket. The replacement is stricter, not looser — it keeps "no spec weakened" and adds an enumeration duty the original did not impose.

## Out of Scope

- Changing `Main.mjs#getNativeWindowRoute`, its privacy, or any of its eight call sites.
- The multi-step compensating park/reshow transaction (`resumeWindowDrag` → orphan-recovery probe → resize → move with two-level rollback). That is the *second* half of #18460's bucket-2 prerequisite and is a separate, larger question about whether `VesselPark` should own a transaction skeleton. **This ticket is the authority half only.**
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/Placement.mjs`'s route-identity comparison.
- Any new native-window capability, or granting a capability any consumer does not already hold.
- Consumer-side refactoring beyond replacing the guard call.

## Avoided Traps

- **Exposing `Main`'s predicate as the "obvious" fix** — it answers a main-thread question; publishing it invites App-Worker callers to cache main-thread truth, the exact staleness §2.8.5 prevents.
- **A generic "window capability service"** — the measured need is one predicate over data an existing owner already holds. A new service would be a second native authority, which ADR 0029 and #18460 both forbid.
- **Naming a class and file before the owner** — #18460's withdrawn prescription is the local precedent for why this body names a responsibility and an evidenced candidate with its falsifier, not a path.
- **Treating this as consumer cleanup** — two of the three sites are dock consumers and it would read as a dock-consumer problem, except the third is `src/ai/client/`. The third site is why this is an engine ticket.
- **Counting `Placement.mjs` to make the number bigger** — it reads `nativeRoute` but guards nothing; folding it in would inflate the evidence and change the ticket's subject.

## Prior decision this ticket must answer to

@neo-gpt-emmy measured the shared native-route responsibility on 2026-09-06 with a four-arm prototype probe across both dock consumers and recorded it on #18304 ([IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABS41lxQ](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18304#issuecomment-5562525125)), explicitly as *evidence to preserve substantial body ownership as unresolved*, and explicitly **not** as grounds for a small symptom ticket. That disposition was correct on its evidence: two dock consumers sharing a shape is a dock-decomposition question, and #18304 owns dock decomposition.

**What changed is the third site.** `src/ai/client/RuntimeService.mjs` re-derives the same predicate with no relationship to the dock, which moves the question outside #18304's subject — the reason this is filed rather than folded onto that epic. The park/reshow *transaction* ownership she measured stays where she put it: unresolved on #18304, and out of scope here.
